# 195 — explainer: pool-detail printed non-EVM token addresses in full

**Tier: HIGH** (user-facing behaviour on the north-star surface; code + tests over the LOW lane's
150-line cap). Full walkthrough + quiz per NORTH_STAR.md's risk policy.

## Goal

The "Underlying Assets" row on pool-detail — the page the `?pool=` / `/tokens/` SEO traffic lands on —
rendered a tidy `0xdac1...1ec7 ↗` chip for an Ethereum address and a raw 44-character base58 blob for a
Solana one. Same information, same row, two completely different treatments, decided by an accident of
which prefix the string happened to start with.

## Intuition

The old code asked one question: *does this string start with `0x` and is it at least 40 characters?* That
question is not "is this an address" — it is "is this an **Ethereum** address". Every other chain fell
through to a branch that had never been designed for addresses at all: the plain-text span meant for
short symbol names.

The fix replaces the yes/no question with a small classifier that answers two questions at once:

1. **Is this address-shaped?** (→ does it get the chip treatment)
2. **Do we know where it resolves?** (→ may the chip be a link, and to which explorer)

Separating those two questions is what makes the honest answer expressible. Before, a token was either a
linked EVM chip or raw text; there was no way to say *"this is clearly an address, truncate it, but I
don't know an explorer for this chain."* That third state is now `href: null` — a chip that looks like a
chip and links nowhere, which is strictly better than a chip that links to a `blockscan.com` 404.

## What changed and why

### `PoolDetail.js` — new helper `classifyUnderlyingToken(token, chain)`

Six rules, first match wins:

| # | shape | address | href |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ethereum:0x…` (chain-prefixed EVM) | the bare `0x…` | blockscan |
| 2 | `0x…` ≥40 chars (bare EVM) | token | blockscan |
| 3 | Solana base58, 32–44 chars, **on chain `Solana`** | token | solscan |
| 4 | Tron `T` + 33 base58, **on chain `Tron`** | token | tronscan |
| 5 | any other opaque id ≥32 chars, no whitespace | token | **`null`** |
| 6 | everything else | — | not a chip |

Two boundaries carry the whole design:

- **Rules 3/4 are chain-gated.** A base58 string is only read as a Solana mint when the pool is actually
  on Solana. Without that gate the classifier would happily send a Stellar contract id to Solscan.
- **Rule 5's 32-character floor** is the anti-over-reach boundary. Solana's shortest legal base58 address
  is 32 characters; every human-readable id measured in the 740-pool snapshot
  (`coingecko:openeden-tbill` at 24, `coingecko:ondo-us-dollar-yield` at 30) sits below it. Drop that
  floor and the page starts truncating slugs that carry their meaning in their text — destroying
  information instead of tidying it.

### `PoolDetail.js` — the render block

The three variants now share **one** `chipStyle` object (the pre-existing EVM anchor style, verbatim —
zero new CSS, zero new tokens, per the 2026-07-10 reuse directive):

- linked chip → `<a>`, `color: var(--color-primary)`, `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, ` ↗`
- unlinked chip → `<span>`, `color: var(--color-text)` — a non-link must not *look* like a link, so it
  keeps the plain-text colour and drops the `↗`
- non-chip → the untouched original plain span, full text, no `title`

Both chip variants carry `title` = the full original token, so the complete address is one hover away and
nothing is actually lost by truncating.

`addressCount` — which drives the pre-existing "swap the truncation for `pool.symbol`'s parts when the
counts line up" shortcut — now counts **all** chip-classified tokens rather than only EVM ones. For a
pool with only EVM tokens the count is identical by construction (rules 1–2 *are* the old test), so that
path is unchanged; for a two-token Solana LP it now shows `SOL ↗` / `USDC ↗` instead of two base58 blobs.

### Everything else

- `PoolDetail.compiled.js` / `.min.js` regenerated (`npm run compile && npm run minify`) — the browser
  loads the minified artifact, not the source, so a stale artifact would mean the fix simply isn't live.
- `package.json` — the new test registered in `test:serial` (`run-tests.js` parses that chain as its file
  list; an unregistered test never runs).
- `test_pool_underlying_address.js` — rendered Playwright, port 8868, all 12 acceptance criteria.

## Diff in reading order

1. `PoolDetail.js` — `classifyUnderlyingToken` added beside `getPoolTypeShared`, with the comment
   explaining why blockscan must never receive a non-EVM address.
2. `PoolDetail.js` — the `underlyingTokens.map(...)` block rewritten around it.
3. `test_pool_underlying_address.js` — the rendered acceptance suite.
4. `package.json` — one-line test registration.
5. `PoolDetail.compiled.js` / `.min.js` — generated, never hand-edited.
6. `product-loop-kit/specs/195.md`, `195-notes.md`, this file, `BACKLOG.md`, `LOG.md` — bookkeeping,
   in the same commit per the 2026-07-13 rule.

## Deviations from the spec

One, documented in `195-notes.md`: the test's fixture pools use **two-part symbols**
(`'JITOSOL/SOL'` rather than the real pool's `'JITOSOL'`). The pre-existing symbol-derivation shortcut
fires whenever `symbolParts.length === addressCount`, which for a real single-token pool always swaps the
symbol in and makes the truncation format unobservable. The addresses themselves are real, copied from
`data/pools-snapshot.json` and asserted present there before the test runs. This is a fixture choice to
make the truncation path observable, not a product-behaviour difference.

A second, smaller one: criterion 8's layout check finds the chip row by walking from the "Underlying
Assets" heading to its `nextElementSibling`, because that row has no class today and adding one would be
an unrequested CSS-surface change. More brittle to unrelated DOM changes than a class selector would be —
stated rather than hidden.

## Known limits, stated

- Explorer coverage stops at Solana and Tron. Stellar Soroban ids and Stacks principals get the chip and
  no link (rule 5) — correct-but-incomplete, and deliberately out of scope.
- The full ~110-file suite was not run; the named regression set was. Stated, not implied.
- No isolable funnel metric. This ships under the 2026-07-23 pre-traffic **quality** mandate, not as a
  conversion experiment; the measurement is the rendered assertion plus the audit scanner staying quiet
  on this surface.

## Quiz

1. The old gate was `token.startsWith('0x') && token.length >= 40`. What question was it *actually*
   answering, and why did that make the Solana render a foregone conclusion rather than a bug someone
   introduced?
2. Rule 5 chips an opaque id but sets `href: null`. Why is that strictly better than pointing it at
   `blockscan.com/address/<id>` — and what would a user experience in each case?
3. Rule 5's threshold is 32 characters. Name the two populations that boundary separates, with an example
   of each from the snapshot, and say what breaks if the number is lowered to 20.
4. `addressCount` changed from counting EVM addresses to counting all chip-classified tokens. Explain why
   this is provably a no-op for a pool whose tokens are all `0x…` addresses.
5. Why does editing `PoolDetail.js` alone leave the production site unchanged, and which command closes
   that gap?
